title: Service principal lifecycle: guided creation, expiry/rotation, owner transfer, and template library
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers and internal platform teams need a predictable, auditable lifecycle for long-lived non-human identities (service principals/service accounts). Current gaps: no enforced expiry or rotation defaults, ambiguous owner transfer UX when the original owner leaves, and inconsistent templating that causes overprivileged accounts. This ticket defines a cross-cutting implementation for: (1) guided creation UX/CLI with templated least-privilege roles, (2) default expiry and rotation policies with reminders and forced rotation path, (3) owner transfer workflow with audit trail and optional delegation, and (4) hooks to include audit logging + SSO/SAML provisioning mapping for org-managed service principals.
acceptance_criteria: New service principal creation flow in Console and CLI that surfaces vetted template choices and explains scope implications
Templates are stored as versioned JSON objects and can be tagged (e.g., data-readonly, model-infer, infra-deploy)
Default expiry (90 days) applied to newly created service principals unless overridden by a user with appropriate privileges; override requires explicit justification logged
Rotation flow: owner can trigger rotation; system supports automated secret rotation with CPI (commit-to-production) webhook to downstream consumers and emits audit events
Owner transfer flow: current owner (or org-admin) can initiate transfer; transfer requires two-step confirmation and is recorded in audit logs including before/after owners
Audit logs include creation template used, expiry/rotation schedule, owner transfer events, and SSO/SAML provisioning source when applicable
CLI and Console expose a way to simulate the effective permissions of a template (dry-run) and show risk score
Backward compatibility with existing service accounts: migration tool to apply default expiry and suggest templates without breaking existing tokens
Unit and integration tests cover template validation, expiry enforcement, rotation webhooks, and audit logging events
tasks: Design: Wireframes for console create flow and owner-transfer modal (work with Design)
API: New endpoints for template CRUD, preview effective permissions, set expiry and rotation schedule
Runtime: Enforcement checks in auth layer to reject token minting beyond expiry and to route rotation requests to dedicated rotation worker
Backend: Store template metadata in tenant config store with versioning and tag indexes
Audit: Define structured audit event schema (service_principal.created, .rotated, .owner_transferred) and wire to ELK/Cloud logging
SSO: Map SAML provisioning attributes (eduPersonPrincipalName, custom attributes) to service principal ownership and source-of-truth bootstrapping
CLI: Add flags --template, --expires-in, --owner and dry-run preview output
Migration: Script to scan existing service principals, surface ones without owners or expiry and create migration tasks
Docs: Draft runbook for oncall and admin teams for forced-transfer and emergency-rotation scenarios
notes: Related artifacts: design mockups in Figma (/redwood/design/rbac/service-principal-create-v2); API spec draft in docs repo (confluence link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/security/rbac-v2/service-principal-lifecycle); initial GH proposal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2456. Coordination required with IAM and Console teams; schedule syncs with Legal for retention/expiry policy alignment.
implementation_decisions: We will adopt a hybrid enforcement model: soft defaults for Hosted tier (notifications + recommended rotation) and hard enforcement for Dedicated/Private when tenant config mandates expiry. Templates will be declarative and validated against a capability matrix; template editing will produce a new template version rather than mutating history to preserve auditability.
risks: Potential breakage for long-lived internal integrations if migration applies expiry without a migration path. UX confusion if templates are too granular; mitigation: provide curated starter templates and a permission preview. SAML mapping complexity across customers — start with enablement for 'SCIM-like' provisioning and iterate.
test_plan_summary: Unit tests for template validation and API; e2e tests for console create flow; integration tests for audit event emission and log ingestion; staging run of migration script against snapshot tenant with feature flag. Load test rotation worker with 10k rotations/hour to validate scaling.
migration_notes: Migration tool will produce a report CSV with suggested template matches, owner candidates, and recommended expiry. We will run in 'dry-run' to surface risky targets then schedule phased enforcement with opt-out window per tenant.
